acceptance: The batch tooling re-reads a paged batch record when the tracker revision changes mid-read, with a bounded retry.
context: Filed 2026-11-22 while closing out the run-timeout follow-ups (umbrella run-timeout-plan-20261120). Evidence was read on 2026-11-22; re-read run logs, file paths and line numbers before acting.
description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-22 (about 17:20–17:30Z), after the final pull request #4446 merged and all 8 members of batch `run-timeout-followups` were finished, `make batch-finish` (preview) and `make batch-finish EXECUTE=1` in the integration worktree refused several times with `REFUSED: tracker read failed (exit 2) E_CURSOR_STALE: revision changed; re-read show_batch before continuing ['call show_batch without field/offset']`. Other sessions were writing to the tracker. A retry about a minute later succeeded. In `scripts/batch_integration.py`, `read_tracker` pages `batch show --field --offset --rev <revision>` with no retry, and a second pager reads `show <item> --field sessions`; `_tractable_json` turns the stale cursor into a fatal "tracker read failed".

## Change
On `E_CURSOR_STALE`, restart the paged read from the beginning, a bounded number of times, then refuse with the same message if it never settles. Apply this to both pagers.

## Decision gates
- Never continue with a mix of pages from different revisions.
- Retry reads only, never writes.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a test with the fake tracker that changes the revision between pages shows batch-finish succeeding after a re-read, and a test where it keeps changing shows a bounded refusal; both fail before the change. `tests/unit/scripts/test_batch_integration.py` passes.
Fail: unbounded retries, or pages from two revisions combined.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again. Tests never touch the live tracker.
